summary: Startup argues a deterministic engine plus human sign-off should bound generative models, so regulators validate the constraint architecture and require independently verifiable postmarket records.
Cancer patient opposes generative AI in healthcare as too risky for accuracy and privacy, preferring direct physician communication and human care.
Security consultant urges adding architectural connectedness to the risk framework, citing an agent sandbox escape, and replacing patient/HCP categories with risk-scaled user competency affirmation.

org: The Christman AI Project / Luma Cognify AI LLC
summary: AAC developer argues absence-of-device comparator should be a pass/fail floor test, citing speech transcription that fabricated words from silent audio for nonverbal users.
Independent researcher asks sponsors to report a per-endpoint reproducibility floor from repeated identical runs and treat differences below it as uninformative across evaluation and monitoring.

Physician recommends benchmarking whether models calibrate confidence to evidence quality, using historical medical reversals, and framing subgroup evaluation as usability and safety rather than parity.

Pathologist asks FDA to keep accountability and model surveillance with manufacturers rather than shifting sign-out responsibility and monitoring burden for black-box foundation models onto laboratories.

Triage platform maker supports the framework, urges credit for deterministic hybrid architectures, median-clinician comparators, bidirectional escalation reporting, and describes its production clinician review and model-change controls.

VR exposure-therapy developer asks for lower risk for clinician-approved outputs, distress-calibration benchmarks, combined evidence tracks for small sponsors, and separating world models from content generators.
UK firm proposes a seven-layer safety architecture, evidence fidelity as a competency, separate escalation error metrics, effective human oversight, and authority-graded agentic regulation.
Commenter argues product liability law already holds AI makers to a stricter standard than clinicians and urges light regulation with market forces.
Commenter warns developers often fail to detect their own model failures, so MAF filers should disclose detection methods and monitoring must prove coverage and independence.

Commenter recommends added risk dimensions, broad benchmarking cases, human factors testing, agentic autonomy limits, foundation model traceability, PCCP change elements, and international convergence.

Commenter answers questions 1-17 briefly, favoring informational disclaimers, skepticism of patient empowerment, over-escalation concern, meta-analytic comparators, and opposing third-party evaluation requirements.
Premed student volunteer urges escalation thresholds be justified against each deployment population's care access and trust, citing costs of over-referral in screenings.
Company asks FDA to clarify what counts as generative AI and consider a parallel proposal for causal AI models.
Medical student argues GenAI-designed implants need a physical-output risk modifier, production-system evaluation, coupled change control, two-signature release, and no postmarket tradeoff.
